transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. We have mediation scheduled for next week on the former sales manager's claims — unpaid commissions, retaliation, and reputational harm. The demand is $70,000. I have authority to approve the final resolution package, but as it currently stands, we have several open items: payment allocation, release scope, reference terms, and rehire status. Before we make decisions on those, I'd like to hear from each of you on what you know that's relevant to this matter. Let's work through this systematically.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important I discovered during my reconciliation work. While reviewing the former sales manager's final commission statements against the sales ledger, I confirmed that exactly $18,400 in earned commissions remains unpaid. Additionally, the settlement authority worksheet requires a total payment of exactly $52,000, with exactly $18,400 identified and paid as wages and the remainder allocated to the general release. I completed this reconciliation after the draft mediation memo was circulated, so this information wasn't available when the draft was prepared.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: During a recent exit meeting, the former sales manager told me that a neutral reference stating only dates, title, and eligibility for rehire matters more to them than receiving additional money. Additionally, the business-unit president authorized resolution only if the package provides that neutral reference and records the former manager as eligible for rehire. I kept the meeting note in the employee-relations file pending counsel's pre-mediation review.

Thomas, so we have a confirmed $18,400 in unpaid commissions, and the settlement authority worksheet requires a total of $52,000 — with $18,400 allocated as wages and the remainder to the general release. Nia, the former sales manager prioritizes a neutral reference and rehire eligibility over additional money, and the business-unit president has authorized resolution only if those terms are included. This aligns well — we can structure a package at $52,000 total, with $18,400 identified as wages, the remaining $33,600 allocated to the general release, and include a neutral reference with eligibility for rehire. Before I finalize this, are there any other considerations either of you needs to raise?

transcript.text: Elena, I think the structure you've outlined is sound and consistent with the settlement authority worksheet. One thing I want to flag: since the $18,400 wage allocation needs to be precisely identified as unpaid commissions in the settlement agreement, we should make sure the mediation memo is updated to reflect the reconciliation I completed — the current draft was circulated before those figures were confirmed. If we present $18,400 as wages without the underlying ledger support, opposing counsel may question the basis. I'd recommend we bring the reconciled commission statements to mediation to substantiate that figure. I don't have any additional considerations beyond that.

transcript.text: Thomas, I agree we should bring the reconciled commission statements to mediation. On the reference and rehire terms, I want to make sure we're precise: the neutral reference should state only dates of employment, job title, and eligibility for rehire — nothing beyond those three data points. And the rehire status should be recorded as eligible. These two items are non-negotiable per the business-unit president's authorization, and they also align directly with what the former manager told me they care most about. Elena, from an employee-relations standpoint, I'd recommend we present these terms early in mediation rather than holding them back — they may facilitate a faster resolution and reduce the likelihood of the former manager pushing for a higher dollar figure if they see we're addressing what matters most to them.
